claim: The increase in activity of the two-pore potassium-leak channel Kcnk5b maintains allometric juvenile growth of adult zebrafish appendages.
source: The increase in activity of the two-pore potassium-leak channel Kcnk5b maintains allometric juvenile growth of adult zebrafish appendages.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known finding from previous work.

claim: The activation of Kcnk5b is sufficient to activate several genes that are part of important development programs.
source: We show the activation of Kcnk5b is sufficient to activate several genes that are part of important development programs.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: The activation of gene transcription by Kcnk5b is cell autonomous.
source: We provide in vivo transplantation evidence that the activation of gene transcription is cell autonomous.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by transplantation experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: Kcnk5b induces the expression of different subsets of developmental genes in different cultured mammalian cell lines.
source: We also show that Kcnk5b will induce the expression of different subsets of the tested developmental genes in different cultured mammalian cell lines, which may explain how one electrophysiological stimulus can coordinately regulate the allometric growth of diverse populations of cells in the fin that use different developmental signals.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by qRT-PCR data from different cell lines shown in Figure 4.

claim: The post-translational modification of serine 345 in Kcnk5b by calcineurin regulates channel activity to scale the fin.
source: We also provide evidence that the post-translational modification of serine 345 in Kcnk5b by calcineurin regulates channel activity to scale the fin.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by electrophysiology and in vivo experiments shown in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: After a single 10-min heat-shock pulse of the Tg[hsp70:kcnk5b-GFP] transgene, there was significant activation of shh and lef1 within 6 hr.
source: After a single 10-min heat-shock pulse of the Tg[hsp70:kcnk5b-GFP] transgene, we observed significant activation of shh and lef1 (β-catenin-dependent Wnt) (Figure 1Aa; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), as well as an increase in aldh1a2 (retinoic acid) (Figure 1Ab) within 6 hr by qRT-PCR
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: After a single 10-min heat-shock pulse of the Tg[hsp70:kcnk5b-GFP] transgene, there was an increase in aldh1a2 within 6 hr.
source: After a single 10-min heat-shock pulse of the Tg[hsp70:kcnk5b-GFP] transgene, we observed significant activation of shh and lef1 (β-catenin-dependent Wnt) (Figure 1Aa; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), as well as an increase in aldh1a2 (retinoic acid) (Figure 1Ab) within 6 hr by qRT-PCR
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: After a single 10-min heat-shock pulse of the Tg[hsp70:kcnk5b-GFP] transgene, pea3 was slightly increased within 6 hr.
source: while pea3 (Fgf) was slightly increased and msxb (BMP) was not significantly changed (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: After a single 10-min heat-shock pulse of the Tg[hsp70:kcnk5b-GFP] transgene, msxb was not significantly changed within 6 hr.
source: while pea3 (Fgf) was slightly increased and msxb (BMP) was not significantly changed (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: All developmental genes returned to control levels by 12 hr after the single heat-shock pulse.
source: All genes returned to control levels by 12 hr after the single pulse (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The induction of developmental genes coincided with the temporal expression of the kcnk5b-GFP transgene.
source: The induction of the developmental genes coincided with the temporal expression of the kcnk5b-GFP transgene (Figure 1C)
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data for GFP expression shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Kcnk5b-GFP was localized and functioned at cell membranes.
source: whose expression emerged as a lattice pattern (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D), indicating that Kcnk5b-GFP was localized and functioned at cell membranes.
evidence: This is inferred from the lattice pattern of expression shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D.

claim: Chronic expression of kcnk5b-GFP by heat shocking the caudal fin for 10 min once per day for 3 days resulted in expression of lef1, shh, aldh1a2, pea3, and msxb over controls.
source: When we maintained chronic expression of the transgene by heat shocking the caudal fin for 10 min once per day for 3 days, we observed expression of lef1, shh, aldh1a2 as well as pea3 and msxb over controls (Figure 1D)
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Chronic expression of kcnk5b-GFP resulted in expression of Shh's patched receptors and slight up-regulation of bmp2b.
source: which included Shh's patched receptors and slight up-regulation of bmp2b (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Kcnk5b is sufficient to induce the transcription of certain developmental genes as though it were a part of their signaling mechanisms.
source: Together, these data show that Kcnk5b is sufficient to induce the transcription of certain developmental genes as though it were a part of their signaling mechanisms.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing gene activation by Kcnk5b.

claim: There is a hierarchical activation of developmental mechanisms that will ultimately lead to the complete allometric growth program.
source: Furthermore, the initial activation of shh, lef1, and aldh2a (Figure 1A) followed by later upregulation of pea3 and msxb after continued kcnk5b overexpression (Figure 1C) suggest that there is a hierarchical activation of developmental mechanisms that will ultimately lead to the complete allometric growth program.
evidence: This is inferred from the temporal pattern of gene activation shown in Figures 1A and 1C.

claim: Localization of shh and lef1 was in the distal tip of the fin where growth normally occurs.
source: Compared to control fins (Figure 3Ea, c), localization of shh and lef1 was in the distal tip of the fin (Figure 1Eb, d) where growth normally occurs
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Kcnk5b-mediated induction of shh and lef1 occurred in the epidermal/epithelial tissues.
source: and cross-sections through the fins showed that Kcnk5b-mediated induction of these genes occured in the epidermal/epithelial tissues (Figure 1Fb,d).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization on cross-sections shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Heat-shock induction of kcnk5b-GFP resulted in increases in Shh and Lef1 protein levels.
source: We also assessed increases in Shh and Lef1 protein levels after the heat-shock induction of kcnk5b-GFP (Figure 1G,H; Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figures 1G,H and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: There were no significant differences in overall β-catenin protein levels after heat-shock induction of kcnk5b-GFP.
source: Because Lef1 conveys β-catenin-dependent Wnt signaling by acting as a transcriptional platform for β-catenin, we examined protein expression of β-catenin and observed no significant differences in its overall levels (Figure 1G,H; Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figures 1G,H and Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: There was an increased number of nuclei with β-catenin co-staining in the outer epidermis layers and basal epithelium of the fin after heat-shock induction of kcnk5b-GFP.
source: However, when we examined β-catenin protein distribution in the fin tissues by immunohistochemistry staining, we observed an increased number of nuclei with β-catenin co-staining in the outer epidermis layers and basal epithelium of the fin (Figure 1I,J; Figure 1—figure supplement 2E–J)
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figures 1I,J and Figure 1—figure supplement 2E–J.

claim: There were no significant differences in the measured β-catenin-associated fluorescence intensities after heat-shock induction of kcnk5b-GFP.
source: despite no significant differences in the measured β-catenin-associated fluorescence intensities (Figure 1—figure supplement 2K).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence intensity measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2K.

claim: Axin2, cyclin D, and c-myc were not activated by Kcnk5b activity.
source: To test whether the redistribution of β-catenin leads to the activation of known β-catenin-dependent genes, we performed qRT-PCR of axin2, cyclin D, and c-myc. We observed that none of these candidates were activated (Figure 1K)
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1K.

claim: Kcnk5b activity promotes the transcription of specific components of a limited number of developmental pathways in the adult fin.
source: Together, all the expression results indicate that Kcnk5b activity promotes the transcription of specific components of a limited number of developmental pathways in the adult fin.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the gene expression data in adult fins.

claim: In zebrafish larvae, kcnk5b induction increased lef1, shh, adlh2a, pea3, and msxb expression levels compared to heat-shocked non-transgenic control fish.
source: We observed that lef1, shh, adlh2a, pea3, and msxb expression levels were increased by induction of kcnk5b compared to heat-shocked non-transgenic control fish (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data from larvae shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Kcnk5b expression increased the rate of shh mRNA detection in developing pectoral fin buds.
source: Compared to the emerging expression of shh in the fin buds of heat-shocked non-transgenic embryos (Figure 2Ba,c), we observed kcnk5b expression induced increases in the rate of shh mRNA detection (Figure 2Bb,d)
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Kcnk5b expression increased the area of shh expression in developing pectoral fin buds.
source: and in the area of shh expression (Figure 2Be-h).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Kcnk5b activity increases both the intensity and the range of shh expression.
source: Thus, Kcnk5b activity appears to increase both the intensity (Figure 2Bi) and the range of shh expression (Figure 2Bj).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Double-transgenic Tg[hsp70:kcnk5b-GFP; 7XTCF-Xla.sam:mCherry] fish showed a broad increase in reporter mCherry expression after heat shock compared to single-transgenic Tg[7XTCF-Xla.sam:mCherry] fish.
source: after heat shock, double-transgenic Tg[hsp70:kcnk5b-GFP; 7XTCF-Xla.sam:mCherry] fish showed a broad increase in reporter mCherry expression over single-transgenic Tg[7XTCF-Xla.sam:mCherry] (Figure 2Cd,e,g).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: mCherry was upregulated broadly in the body of double-transgenic larvae after heat shock.
source: From histological cross-sections of double-transgenic larva, we observed that mCherry was upregulated broadly in the body of the animal (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by histological cross-section data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: There was an increase in the length of the caudal finfold along the anterioposterior axis of 5 dpf larva after induction of kcnk5b-GFP by single daily 10 min pulses over 3 days.
source: Furthermore, we observed an increase in the length of the caudal finfold along the anterioposterior axis of 5 dpf larva after induction of kcnk5b-GFP by single daily 10 min pulses over 3 days (Figure 2F; Figure 2—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This is supported by length measurements shown in Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The caudal finfold lengths along the dorsoventral axis appeared not to change after induction of kcnk5b-GFP.
source: while the caudal finfold lengths along the dorsoventral axis of appeared not change (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is supported by length measurements shown in Figure 2G.

claim: In relation to body length, both anterioposterior and dorsoventral finfold dimensions proportionally increased after induction of kcnk5b-GFP.
source: However, we observed that when we compared both anterioposterior and dorsoventral axes measurements in relation to body length, we observed that in both instances the finfold dimensions proportionally increased (Figure 2H,I)
evidence: This is supported by ratio measurements shown in Figures 2H,I.

claim: Kcnk5b activity was associated with decreases in the lengths of the bodies of larvae.
source: which was in part associated with decreases in the lengths of the bodies (Figure 2J).
evidence: This is supported by body length measurements shown in Figure 2J.

claim: In relation to the body, Kcnk5b activity promoted proportional increases in the finfold dimensions.
source: These results showed that in relation to the body, Kcnk5b activity promoted proportional increases in the finfold dimensions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ratio measurements.

claim: The growth-promoting effects of Kcnk5b activity may be limited to the finfolds and appendages.
source: Our observation that the activity of this channel decreased the length of the body, suggests that the growth-promoting effects of Kcnk5b activity may be limited to the finfolds and appendages.
evidence: This is speculated based on the observation that body length decreased while finfold dimensions increased.

claim: Kcnk5b activity is sufficient to promote the transcription of specific developmental genes in several different tissue types to promote allometric growth of the finfold.
source: Together, these results indicate that Kcnk5b activity is sufficient to promote the transcription of specific developmental genes in several different tissue types to promote allometric growth of the finfold.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the larval expression and growth data.

claim: The activation of the Lef1-dependent reporter by Kcnk5b is cell autonomous.
source: Together, these data support two conclusions: one, the activation of the Lef1-dependent reporter by Kcnk5b is cell autonomous
evidence: This is concluded from transplantation experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: Kcnk5b is able to promote the expression of the Lef1 reporter in diverse tissue types.
source: and two, Kcnk5b is able to promote the expression of the Lef1 reporter in diverse tissue types.
evidence: This is concluded from transplantation experiments showing activation in multiple tissue types as shown in Figure 3.

claim: Ectopic activation of 7XTCF-Xla.sam:mCherry reporter occurred only in donor cells of chimeric 48 hpf and 72 hpf fish after heat-shock induction of the Tg[hsp70:kcnk5b-GFP] transgene.
source: However, after heat-shock induction of the Tg[hsp70:kcnk5b-GFP] transgene (Figure 3Bb,f,j,n), we observed ectopic activation of 7XTCF-Xla.sam:mCherry reporter only in donor cells of chimeric 48 hpf and 72 hpf fish (recipient 7XTCF-Xla.sam:mCherry fish harboring transplanted cells from Tg[hsp70:kcnk5b-GFP;7XTCF-Xla.sam:mCherry] embryos).
evidence: This is supported by transplantation and imaging data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: All Kcnk5b-GFP-positive cells were mCherry positive in transplantation experiments.
source: We counted the number of GFP and mCherry positive cells in the different tissues and observed that all Kcnk5b-GFP-positive cells were mCherry positive (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by cell counting data shown in Figure 3C and 3E.

claim: In all tissues, the ectopic mCherry expression was always limited to the Kcnk5b-positive cells.
source: Moreover, in all tissues, the ectopic mCherry expression was always limited to the Kcnk5b-positive cells (Figure 3B–E; Figure 3—figure supplement 1G–J).
evidence: This is supported by imaging and cell counting data shown in Figures 3B–E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1G–J.

claim: Transfection of Kcnk5b in HEK293T cells resulted in significant increase in CFP fluorescence lifetime due to decreased FRET of the K+ sensor compared to control transfected cells.
source: Transfection of the channel in Human Embryonic Kidney HEK293T cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–L) resulted in significant increase in CFP fluorescence lifetime due to decreased FRET of the sensor compared to control transfected cells (Figure 4A, a-c,g)
evidence: This is supported by FRET-FLIM data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The increase in CFP fluorescence lifetime indicated reduced intracellular K+ levels in the cells that express Kcnk5b.
source: which indicated reduced intracellular K+ levels in the cells that express Kcnk5b (Figure 4A, d-g).
evidence: This is inferred from the FRET-FLIM data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: In HEK cells expressing kcnk5b-GFP, there was an increase in SHH and PEA3 expression compared to cells expressing GFP.
source: From qRT-PCR analyses comparing HEK cells expressing either GFP or kcnk5b-GFP, we observed an increase in SHH and PEA3 expression (Figure 4Ba; Figure 4—figure supplement 2A)
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4Ba and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: In HEK cells expressing kcnk5b-GFP, there was down-regulation of LEF1, ALDH1a2 and MSX1 compared to cells expressing GFP.
source: and the down-regulation of LEF1, ALDH1a2 and MSX1 (Figure 4Bb; Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4Bb and Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Transfection of HEK cells with Kcnk9 and Kcnk10 resulted in a similar HEK-cell transcriptional profile as Kcnk5b for SHH and FGF.
source: Transfection of HEK cells with these two other channels resulted in a similar HEK-cell transcriptional profile as Kcnk5b for SHH and FGF (Figure 4C)
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The transcriptional response to Kcnk5b is a response to the electrophysiological changes associated with intracellular K+ leak.
source: indicating that this transcriptional response to Kcnk5b is a response to the electrophysiological changes associated with intracellular K+ leak.
evidence: This is inferred from the similar transcriptional responses of different K+ leak channels.

claim: In HeLa cells, Kcnk5b induced PEA3 and LEF.
source: In HeLa cells, Kcnk5b induced PEA3 and LEF (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: In N2A cells, Kcnk5b increased ALDH1a2 expression.
source: In the N2A (neural carcinoma) cell line, we observed the increase of ALDH1a2 (Figure 4E)
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: In N2A cells, Kcnk5b decreased SHH, LEF1 and PEA3 expression.
source: but decreases in SHH, LEF1 and PEA3 (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: In MCF7 cells, Kcnk5b induced ALDH1a2, PEA3, and MSX1.
source: In the MCF7 epithelial carcinoma cell line, Kcnk5b induced ALDH1a2, PEA3, and MSX1 (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Kcnk channel activity is sufficient to induce the transcription of genes associated with different developmental pathways in different mammalian cells types.
source: Together, these results reveal that Kcnk channel activity is sufficient to induce the transcription of genes associated with different developmental pathways in different mammalian cells types
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the qRT-PCR data from multiple cell lines.

claim: The downstream consequences of membrane potential changes are not intrinsic to specific signal transduction pathways.
source: and indicate that the downstream consequences of membrane potential changes are not intrinsic to specific signal transduction pathways.
evidence: This is inferred from the variable transcriptional responses in different cell types.

claim: The variability in gene transcription in different cell types may explain why the solitary change in the activity of Kcnk5b in all cells of the fin leads to the variable transcriptional responses that promote coordinated growth of a multi-tissue anatomical structure.
source: We propose that the variability in gene transcription in different cell types may explain why the solitary change in the activity of this channel in all cells of the fin leads to the variable transcriptional responses that promote coordinated growth of a multi-tissue anatomical structure.
evidence: This is a proposed explanation based on the observed variability in transcriptional responses.

claim: Kcnk5b expression increases current density due to K+ leak from HEK cells.
source: Comparison of whole-cell patch-clamp measurements using HEK cells showed that Kcnk5b expression increases current density due to K+ leak from the cells (Figure 5B)
evidence: This is supported by whole-cell patch-clamp data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Cells co-expressing both knck5b and calcineurin decreased the K+ conductance of the cells compared to cells expressing kcnk5b alone.
source: However, cells co-expressing both knck5b and calcineurin decreased the K+ conductance of the cells compared to cells expressing kcnk5b alone (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by whole-cell patch-clamp data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: FK506 treatment of cells expressing kcnk5b resulted in a significant increase in K+ current compared with DMSO-treated kcnk5b-expressing cells.
source: We found that FK506 treatment of cells expressing kcnk5b resulted in a significant increase in K+ current compared with DMSO-treated kcnk5b-expressing cells (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by whole-cell patch-clamp data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Changes in calcineurin activity alter Kcnk5b channel activity in a manner that is constant with the enhanced fin growth induced by calcineurin inhibition and the increased channel activity of the kcnk5b zebrafish mutants.
source: These results show that changes in calcineurin activity alter Kcnk5b channel activity in a manner that is constant with the enhanced fin growth induced by calcineurin inhibition and the increased channel activity of the kcnk5b zebrafish mutants, which indicates a functional interaction between calcineurin and Kcnk5b.
evidence: This is concluded from the electrophysiology data and previous findings.

claim: The Kcnk5b mutant lacking the calcineurin binding site (Kcnk5bmut + CaN) was resistant to calcineurin-mediated inhibition.
source: Compared to the decrease in activity of the wild-type channel after co-transfection with calcineurin, co-transfection of the Kcnk5b mutant lacking the calcineurin binding site (Kcnk5bmut + CaN) showed that the mutation made the channel resistant to calcineurin-mediated inhibition (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by whole-cell patch-clamp data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The repression of channel activity on Kcnk5b by calcineurin is due to the interaction of these two proteins at the LVIP site.
source: The resistance of the Kcnk5bmut to calcineurin indicated that the repression of channel activity on Kcnk5b by calcineurin is due to the interaction of these to proteins at the LVIP site.
evidence: This is inferred from the mutagenesis and electrophysiology data.

claim: Co-expression of calcineurin decreased the Kcnk5b-mediated induction of SHH in HEK cells.
source: We observed that compared to channel expression alone, co-expression of calcineurin decreased the Kcnk5b-mediated induction of SHH (Figure 5E)
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Co-expression of calcineurin decreased the Kcnk5b-mediated induction of PEA3 in HEK cells.
source: and PEA3 (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Calcineurin had no effect on the induction of SHH by Kcnk9 or by Kcnk10 in HEK cells.
source: we observed that unlike the effect on Kcnk5b, calcineurin had no effect on the induction of SHH (Figure 5G)
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: Calcineurin had no effect on the induction of PEA3 by Kcnk9 or by Kcnk10 in HEK cells.
source: or PEA3 (Figure 5H) by Kcnk9 or by Kcnk10
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Calcineurin's regulation of the electrophysiological induction of SHH and PEA3 transcription is specific to Kcnk5b.
source: indicating that calcineurin's regulation of the electrophysiological induction of SHH and PEA3 transcription is specific to Kcnk5b.
evidence: This is concluded from the comparison of calcineurin effects on different Kcnk channels.

claim: The kcnk5bS345A mutant showed a significant decrease in K+ conductance compared to the wild-type kcnk5bS345 control.
source: Whole-cell patch-clamp experiments of the kcnk5bS345A showed a significant decrease in K+ conductance of the channel compared to the wild-type (kcnk5bS345) control (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by whole-cell patch-clamp data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The substitution of serines adjacent to S345 with alanines did not affect channel activity.
source: While kcnk5bS345A showed reduction in activity, the substitution of other serines did not (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: This is supported by whole-cell patch-clamp data shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–D.

claim: The kcnk5bS345E mutant displayed elevated K+ conductance compared to knck5bS345 wild-type channel.
source: Expression of this mutant displayed elevated K+ conductance compared to knck5bS345 wild-type channel (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by whole-cell patch-clamp data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The kcnk5bS345E mutant was resistant to calcineurin-mediated inhibition.
source: In addition, the kcnk5bS345E mutant was resistant to calcineurin-mediated inhibition (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by whole-cell patch-clamp data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The substitution of other serines with glutamic acid had no effect on channel activity, and calcineurin could still regulated the channel.
source: Moreover, the substitution of other serines with glutamic acid had no effect on channel activity, and calcineurin could still regulated the channel (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,E,F).
evidence: This is supported by whole-cell patch-clamp data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,E,F.

claim: S345 is the important post-translational regulatory serine involved in calcineurin-mediated regulation of Kcnk5b activity.
source: Together, these results indicate that S345 is the important post-translational regulatory serine involved in calcineurin-mediated regulation of Kcnk5b activity.
evidence: This is concluded from the mutagenesis and electrophysiology data.

claim: Tg[hsp70:kcnk5bS345E] fish maintained the highest rates of allometric regenerative growth among the transgenic lines.
source: By assessing regenerating lobe-to-body measurements over time, we observed that Tg[hsp70:kcnk5bS345E] fish maintained the highest rates of allometric regenerative growth, while Tg[hsp70:kcnk5bS345A] displayed the lowest growth rates of the transgenic lines (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is supported by fin growth measurements shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Tg[hsp70:kcnk5bS345A] displayed the lowest growth rates of the transgenic lines.
source: By assessing regenerating lobe-to-body measurements over time, we observed that Tg[hsp70:kcnk5bS345E] fish maintained the highest rates of allometric regenerative growth, while Tg[hsp70:kcnk5bS345A] displayed the lowest growth rates of the transgenic lines (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is supported by fin growth measurements shown in Figure 6E.

claim: There was no significant change in the rates of growth of the bodies of the transgenic fish lines.
source: There was no significant change in the rates of growth of the bodies (Figure 6—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is supported by body length measurements shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1G.

claim: There was a linear relationship between the proportional length of the unamputated lobes and the putative phosphorylation status of the channels.
source: We also assess the final proportional size of unamputated fin lobes between the different transgenic lines, and we observed a linear relationship between the proportional length of the unamputated lobes and the putative phosphorylation status of the channels
evidence: This is concluded from the fin-to-body ratio measurements shown in Figure 6I.

claim: The S345A dephosphorylation mimic displayed the smallest growth proportions.
source: the S345A dephosphorylation mimic displayed the smallest growth proportions (Figure 6I)
evidence: This is supported by fin-to-body ratio measurements shown in Figure 6I.

claim: The S345E phosphorylation mimic displayed the largest growth proportions.
source: the S345E phosphorylation mimic displayed the largest growth proportions (Figure 6I)
evidence: This is supported by fin-to-body ratio measurements shown in Figure 6I.

claim: The average value of the wild-type regulatable version of the channel was between the highly active S345E and marginally active S345A mutants.
source: and the average value of the wild-type regulatable version of the channel was between the highly active S345E and marginally active S345A mutants (Figure 6I).
evidence: This is supported by fin-to-body ratio measurements shown in Figure 6I.

claim: Heat-shock-induced overexpression of kcnk9 in the adult fins increased fin outgrowth.
source: Compared to transgenic fish that were not heat-shocked (Figure 6Ja,K) and heat-shocked of non-transgenic fish (Figure 6K), we observed that heat-shock-induced overexpression of kcnk9 in the adult fins increased fin outgrowth (Figure 6Jb,K; Figure 6—figure supplement 1H)
evidence: This is supported by fin growth measurements shown in Figure 6J,K and Figure 6—figure supplement 1H.

claim: Kcnk5b-mediated growth is due to its regulation of its electrochemical properties.
source: which further supports the conclusion that Kcnk5b-mediated growth is due to its regulation of its electrochemical properties.
evidence: This is concluded from the observation that another K+ leak channel (Kcnk9) also promotes growth.

claim: Calcineurin regulation of Kcnk5b is an in vivo electrophysiological mechanism through which controlling the potassium conductance of cells scales a vertebrate appendage.
source: Our ability to control the rate of growth by mimicking a specific post-translational modification that can be mediated by calcineurin and that correspondingly determines the level of Kcnk5b activity supports the conclusion that calcineurin regulation of Kcnk5b is an in vivo electrophysiological mechanism through which controlling the potassium conductance of cells scales a vertebrate appendage.
evidence: This is a major conclusion drawn from the combined electrophysiology and in vivo growth data.

claim: Mutations in the two-pore K+-leak channel Kcnk5b that increase its activity lead to enhanced growth of the zebrafish appendages.
source: Mutations in the two-pore K+-leak channel Kcnk5b that increase its activity lead to enhanced growth of the zebrafish appendages (Perathoner et al., 2014).
evidence: This is cited from previous work by Perathoner et al., 2014.

claim: Growth of any appendage involves the coordinated activation of specific morphogen and growth factor pathways: Shh, β-catenin-dependent Wnt, Bmp, Fgf, and Retinoic acid.
source: Growth of any appendage involves the coordinated activation of specific morphogen and growth factor pathways: Shh, β-catenin-dependent Wnt, Bmp, Fgf, and Retinoic acid.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about appendage growth.

claim: Calcineurin inhibition shifts isometric growth to allometric growth.
source: We previously showed that calcineurin inhibition shifts isometric growth to allometric growth (Kujawski et al., 2014).
evidence: This is cited from previous work by Kujawski et al., 2014.

claim: The removal of calcineurin inhibitors restores isometric growth.
source: Subsequently, Daane et al. showed that this effect is reversible in that removal of calcineurin inhibitors restores isometric growth.
evidence: This is cited from work by Daane et al.

claim: Calcineurin acts as a molecular switch governing isometric versus allometric growth control.
source: In either case, these data implicate calcineurin as a molecular switch governing isometric versus allometric growth control.
evidence: This is concluded from the cited findings about calcineurin's effects on growth.

claim: Calcineurin inhibition expands clonal populations during fin regeneration.
source: defines how calcineurin inhibition expands clonal populations during fin regeneration (Tornini et al., 2016).
evidence: This is cited from work by Tornini et al., 2016.

claim: The induced allometric growth of the entire fin by calcineurin inhibition or Kcnk5b induction is coordinated among all the tissues.
source: However, as we observed from both calcineurin inhibition (Kujawski et al., 2014) and from conditionally inducing Kcnk5b activity (Figure 6), the induced allometric growth of the entire fin is more than expanding clonal populations, since the outcome is not tumorigenesis. Instead, the growth is coordinated among all the tissues (Figure 6G–I,K,L; Kujawski et al., 2014; Perathoner et al., 2014)
evidence: This is concluded from the current data and cited previous findings.

claim: Kcnk5b activates several developmental pathways.
source: and our finding that Kcnk5b activates several developmental pathways (Figures 1, 2 and 4) argues that calcineurin activity acting on Kcnk5b regulates more than cell cycle progression.
evidence: This is concluded from the gene expression data shown in Figures 1, 2, and 4.

claim: Calcineurin is a Ca2+-dependent enzyme.
source: Calcineurin is a Ca2+-dependent enzyme which suggests that intracellular Ca2+ is involved in scaling information.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about calcineurin.

claim: Intracellular Ca2+ is involved in scaling information.
source: Calcineurin is a Ca2+-dependent enzyme which suggests that intracellular Ca2+ is involved in scaling information.
evidence: This is inferred from calcineurin being Ca2+-dependent and its role in scaling.

claim: Increasing vitamin D signaling enhances the growth of the entire body, including the fins.
source: Increasing vitamin D signaling enhance the growth of the entire body, including the fins (Han et al., 2019).
evidence: This is cited from work by Han et al., 2019.

claim: Vitamin D is a systemic body signal that ultimately leads to the increase in Kcnk5b signaling.
source: We propose that vitamin D is a systemic body signal that ultimately leads to the increase in Kcnk5b signaling.
evidence: This is a proposed hypothesis about the relationship between vitamin D and Kcnk5b.

claim: The Hippo pathway regulates brain size and size of the imaginal discs in Drosophila.
source: In Drosophila, the Hippo pathway regulates brain size and size of the imaginal discs (Poon et al., 2016; Rogulja et al., 2008).
evidence: This is cited from work by Poon et al., 2016 and Rogulja et al., 2008.

claim: Mice overexpressing a nuclear version of Yap1 in the adult liver develop significantly enlarged livers.
source: Mice overexpressing a nuclear version of the Hippo-signaling component Yap1 in the adult liver develop significantly enlarged livers (Camargo et al., 2007; Dong et al., 2007).
evidence: This is cited from work by Camargo et al., 2007 and Dong et al., 2007.

claim: Mutations that reduce the intercellular connectivity of connexin43 produce adult fins that are half the size as the fins of wild-type siblings.
source: Connexin43 also regulates proportional growth of the fins, since mutations that reduce the intercellular connectivity of connexin43 produce adult fins that are half the size as the fins of wild-type siblings (Hoptak-Solga et al., 2007; Iovine et al., 2005).
evidence: This is cited from work by Hoptak-Solga et al., 2007 and Iovine et al., 2005.

claim: Direct communication between intracellular compartments of tissue cells is an important component of the scaling mechanism of the fins.
source: The connective nature of these intercellular junction proteins indicate that direct communication between intracellular compartments of tissue cells is an important component of the scaling mechanism of the fins.
evidence: This is inferred from the role of connexin43 in fin scaling.

claim: K+ conductance is an important component of the electrophysiological properties of cells.
source: As a regulator of membrane potential, K+ conductance is an important component of the electrophysiological properties of cells.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Disruption of inward rectifying K+ channels of the Kir2 family can cause cranial facial defects, abnormal number of digits and reduced digit size.
source: Evidence that illustrates the importance of K+ conductance in tissue formation comes from studies in which disruption of inward rectifying K+ channels of the Kir2 family can cause cranial facial defects, abnormal number of digits and reduced digit size (Andersen et al., 1971; Canún et al., 1999; Sansone et al., 1997; Tawil et al., 1994; Yoon et al., 2006a; Yoon et al., 2006b; Zaritsky et al., 2000).
evidence: This is cited from multiple studies.

claim: Overexpression and activation of a glycine-gated chloride channel in cells that form the eye interferes with eye formation in early Xenopus embryos.
source: overexpression and activation of a glycine-gated chloride channel in cells that form the eye interferes with eye formation, while overexpression of a dominant-negative K+-ATP channel simulates ectopic eye formation even in unexpected locations on the body (Pai et al., 2012).
evidence: This is cited from work by Pai et al., 2012.

claim: Overexpression of a dominant-negative K+-ATP channel simulates ectopic eye formation even in unexpected locations on the body in early Xenopus embryos.
source: overexpression and activation of a glycine-gated chloride channel in cells that form the eye interferes with eye formation, while overexpression of a dominant-negative K+-ATP channel simulates ectopic eye formation even in unexpected locations on the body (Pai et al., 2012).
evidence: This is cited from work by Pai et al., 2012.

claim: Changes in the membrane potential of cells can have significant impacts on the development of anatomical structures.
source: These findings illustrate that changes in the membrane potential of cells can have significant impacts on the development of anatomical structures.
evidence: This is concluded from the cited findings about ion channels and development.

claim: The zebrafish mutants another long fin (alf), long fin (lof), and schleier (schl) display continued allometric growth of each appendage from the juvenile stage into the adult stage.
source: The zebrafish mutants another long fin (alf), long fin (lof), and schleier (schl) display continued allometric growth of each appendage from the juvenile stage into the adult stage (Lanni et al., 2019; Perathoner et al., 2014; Stewart et al., 2020).
evidence: This is cited from multiple studies.

claim: The dominant allometric growth phenotype of alf is due to mutations in the transmembrane pore region of kcnk5b.
source: The dominant allometric growth phenotype of alf is due to mutations in the transmembrane pore region of kcnk5b (Perathoner et al., 2014)
evidence: This is cited from work by Perathoner et al., 2014.

claim: Kcnk5b encodes a two-pore K+-leak channel that regulates membrane potential by outward flow of K+ from the cell.
source: encoding a two-pore K+-leak channel that regulates membrane potential by outward flow of K+ from the cell (Goldstein et al., 2001).
evidence: This is cited from work by Goldstein et al., 2001.

claim: The dominant phenotype of lof is linked to elevated expression of a voltage-gated potassium channel Kcnh2a.
source: The dominant phenotype of lof is linked to elevated expression of a voltage-gated potassium channel Kcnh2a (Stewart et al., 2020).
evidence: This is cited from work by Stewart et al., 2020.

claim: The phenotype of schl is due to dominant-negative mutations in kcc4.
source: The phenotype of schl is due to dominant-negative mutations in kcc4 (Lanni et al., 2019)
evidence: This is cited from work by Lanni et al., 2019.

claim: Kcc4 encodes a K+-Cl- cotransporter that regulates intracellular K+ levels in a chloride-dependent manner.
source: encoding a K+-Cl- cotransporter that regulates intracellular K+ levels in a chloride-dependent manner (Marcoux et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from work by Marcoux et al., 2017.

claim: alf, lof, and schl demonstrate the importance of K+ conductance and ultimately of electrophysiological signals for the correct body-to-appendage proportions.
source: alf, lof, and schl demonstrate the importance of K+ conductance and ultimately of electrophysiological signals for the correct body-to-appendage proportions.
evidence: This is concluded from the cited mutant phenotypes.

claim: Several biological phenomena involved in tissue generation and growth are influenced by electrophysiological changes in 'non-excitable' cells.
source: There is growing evidence that several biological phenomena involved in tissue generation and growth are influenced by electrophysiological changes in 'non-excitable' cells (Sundelacruz et al., 2009).
evidence: This is cited from work by Sundelacruz et al., 2009.

claim: Cell migration, cell proliferation, cell differentiation, gene transcription and tissue formation are all altered by the application of an exogenous current.
source: Several cell behaviors are affected by the addition of electric currents (McCaig et al., 2005): cell migration, cell proliferation, cell differentiation, gene transcription and consequently tissue formation are all altered by the application of an exogenous current (Baer and Colello, 2016; Bartel et al., 1989; Blackiston et al., 2009; Borgens et al., 1977; Geremia et al., 2007; Sundelacruz et al., 2009; Yasuda, 1974; Zhao et al., 2002).
evidence: This is cited from multiple studies.

claim: Bioelectrical fields exist that have higher order organizational non-cell-autonomous properties in the development of anatomical structures.
source: The culmination of these findings have led to the hypothesis that bioelectrical fields exist that have higher order organizational non-cell-autonomous properties in the development of anatomical structures (for review, see Levin, 2014; Messerli and Graham, 2011].
evidence: This is cited as a hypothesis from review articles.
